items.caption: This bronze-style form has a central arm-like stroke and branching strokes above and to the sides. Paleographic accounts interpret the branches as fingers and the lower part as the arm or palm, forming a pictograph of a hand.
items.alt: Black brushlike strokes form a branching hand shape with a long central descending stroke.
items.selection_reason: It illustrates the early bronze-script hand graph and its interpreted anatomy. The image is a modern redraw, while the cited catalogues document bronze forms from the Western Zhou onward.

items.caption: This seal-script form presents 手 with a central vertical stroke and paired curving branches. Shuowen classifies 手 as pictographic and glosses it as 拳, “fist”; that historical lexicographic account does not establish a sequence of meanings.
items.alt: A seal-script character with a central vertical stroke and curved branches on both sides.
items.selection_reason: Together with the bronze-style form, it shows a distinct seal-script representation of the hand graph. It is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact.

limitations.text: The bronze and seal images are modern redrawings rather than photographs of inscriptions. The cited sources interpret the bronze graph as a hand, but its exact anatomy is not certain; the sources differ on whether the lower portion represents an arm or includes the palm. Bronze examples are catalogued from the Western Zhou onward, but no individual earliest inscription date or semantic context is established here.

手 is reported absent from oracle-bone inscriptions in the cited paleographic discussions; those discussions distinguish other hand-shaped graphs, so the selected forms do not establish an oracle-bone 手 form.
